A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CEM study, with complete main text and supplementary Sections 7-12. The text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and supplementary Sections 10-12 report original classification, inversion-reconstruction, hyperparameter and runtime experiments across four datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the quantitative comparisons in Tables 1-9 and analyses in Figures 3-5.

M1.justification: The CEM procedure, Gaussian mixture estimation, noise mechanism, parameter updates and combined training loss remain identical in Algorithm 1 and Sections 3-4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same object-classification and face-recognition coverage: CIFAR10, CIFAR100, TinyImageNet and FaceScrub, under the same inversion scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding tables retain the same comparator membership, including Bottleneck, DistCorr, Dropout, PATROL, ResSFL, Noise_Nopeek and Noise_ARL. The decoding-based and GAN-based attack comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The VGG11/ResNet-20 configurations, data splits, training budgets, white-box access, accuracy/MSE/SSIM/PSNR metrics and runtime evaluation procedure are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the entropy-MSE analysis in Figure 3, noise-strength, loss-weight and partition-depth studies in Figure 4, and reconstruction examples in Figure 5.

E5.justification: Performance tables retain point estimates without added uncertainty intervals or significance tests. Supplementary Section 12 reports the same 100 timing repetitions; no repeated-run or seed information changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1-9 contain identical numerical entries, including supplementary CIFAR100, SSIM/PSNR and efficiency results. The plotted trends and reconstruction examples in Figures 3-5 also match.

T1.justification: Propositions 1-2, Theorems 1-2 and Equations 1-16 retain the same mathematical content, including both proofs in supplementary Sections 7-8.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion preserve the same theoretical-bound and CEM contributions, including the reported 12.9%-48.2% robustness gains and utility/efficiency claims.

C2.justification: The utility-robustness interpretation, shallow-encoder constraints, explanation of FaceScrub vulnerability and hyperparameter interpretations are unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: The hyperparameters, inversion-network architecture and training details, RTX 4090 timing setup, and code-access link remain unchanged in the main text and supplement.

R1.justification: The same 70 works are cited, and the related-work discussion and novelty positioning are unchanged. Expanded venue abbreviations are bibliographic formatting changes.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgement section, updates author spelling, affiliation and contact information, and standardizes reference venue names. The scientific prose and section organization otherwise match.

P2.justification: v2 adjusts page alignment and diagram-label typography, including Figures 2 and 6. The acknowledgment and longer venue names reflow the references; figure and table content, captions and structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new funding acknowledgment improves attribution, while metadata and formatting receive small edits. Both versions provide the same scientific argument, proofs, experimental evidence and reproducibility information, leaving overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
